findings.description: find() returns the same list object that is stored in the cache, on both a hit (line 63) and a miss (line 68). Before this change every call built a fresh list. A caller that sorts, appends to or pops from the result now silently corrupts the cached entry, so later callers with the same query get the modified list.
findings.suggestion: Store the list as a tuple, or return list(entry[1]) and list(hits) so callers get a copy.
findings.title: Cached result list is returned by reference and can be mutated by callers

findings.description: The lookup pops the key before checking the TTL, so an expired entry has already been removed when the size check runs. That is fine. On an expired miss with a full cache, however, the size check can evict an unrelated live entry even though a slot was just freed by the pop. This wastes cache entries.
findings.suggestion: Make the eviction check run only when the key is not already present, or run it after accounting for the popped entry.
findings.title: Expired entry is popped, so cache may be evicted needlessly
